signals.topic: AI assistant gets stuck in repetitive search/read loops consuming excessive tokens with no timeout
signals.summary: The AI repeatedly calls search_files and read_file in tight loops without making progress, consuming high or near-100% token usage, and does not timeout or break out of the loop.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports of the same root cause (AI loop without progress + no timeout). Causes both task blockage and significant token over-consumption. Count=2 meets the threshold. The root cause is shared: the agent lacks effective loop detection or token budget enforcement.

source_issues.title: AI assistant gets stuck in search/read loops with high token usage and no timeout

source_issues.title: Cline repeating to read project_management.md loop

signals.topic: Hook cancel action causes Cline to permanently lock in 'Resume task' state requiring IDE restart
signals.summary: When a PreToolUse hook uses cancel=true, Cline enters a permanent 'Resume task' state where neither clicking the button nor typing input does anything — only full IDE restart works.
signals.review_reason: Core workflow is permanently blocked. The Resume task button becomes completely non-interactive after a hook cancel — this is a full extension lockup requiring IDE restart. High severity despite count=1 because the failure mode is catastrophic (no recovery path within the app) and directly breaks the primary task lifecycle.

source_issues.title: An abort from a hook causes cline to get locked in a "Resume task" state
source_issues.evidence: User reports lockup: hook cancels task → Resume task button appears but is unresponsive → must close/reopen VS Code to recover. Affects core task management workflow.

signals.topic: Rapid sequential file edits cause approval buttons to disappear, softlocking Cline
signals.summary: When Cline edits files one after another in quick succession, the approve/reject buttons do not appear, causing the extension to softlock with no way to proceed.
signals.review_reason: Directly blocks the primary user interaction loop (approve/reject edits). User is forced to reload the extension to recover. This is a main-flow failure with a clear reproduction path and visual evidence.

source_issues.title: Lockup when editing files one after another
source_issues.evidence: User reports: rapid sequential file edits → approve buttons vanish → extension softlocks → must reload. Screenshot provided showing missing buttons.

signals.topic: Response truncation mid-tool-call causes 'You did not use a tool' error loop with no recovery
signals.summary: When context window fills (60-120k tokens), responses get truncated mid-tool-call XML tag, triggering repeated 'You did not use a tool' errors and infinite retry loops, making forward progress impossible.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is blocked — every retry fails identically creating an infinite loop that only user manual intervention can break. Affects the core editing workflow on large files, a common use case. The error message is actively misleading (blames the model for not using a tool when the tool call was simply truncated).

source_issues.title: Cline repeatedly reports "[ERROR] You did not use a tool" when tool calls are present but response is truncated mid-tag
source_issues.evidence: User reports: ~1800-line Python file with multiple edits → context fills → XML closing tag never written → every retry also truncated → infinite error loop → user must manually interrupt and resume.

signals.topic: Internal `task_progress` parameter leaked to MCP servers causing Pydantic validation errors and tool call failures
signals.summary: Cline forwards its internal `task_progress` parameter to MCP servers during tool calls, causing Pydantic-validated servers (e.g. things-mcp) to reject the call with validation errors, breaking all tool operations with that MCP server.
signals.review_reason: Clear technical root cause with a straightforward fix (strip task_progress before forwarding). Breaks the entire MCP tool ecosystem for any server using strict parameter validation — this is a systemic integration failure, not an edge case.

source_issues.title: task_progress parameter is forwarded to MCP servers, breaking things-mcp
source_issues.evidence: things-mcp uses Pydantic parameter validation → rejects unexpected task_progress parameter → every tool call fails. Clear root cause and reproducible with any Pydantic-validated MCP server.

signals.topic: Non-interactive CLI commands fail to authenticate using keychain-stored API key
signals.summary: API keys stored via the interactive /auth command in the system keychain are not accessible to non-interactive commands (e.g., gemini extensions install), causing auth failures despite successful key setup.
aliases: keychain auth not checked for non-interactive commands
signals.review_reason: A core command path (non-interactive extensions install) is completely broken by an auth inconsistency. The user successfully configured the API key through the official interactive flow, but it silently fails for non-interactive use — a clear main-flow failure for a real CLI workflow.

source_issues.title: Non-interactive commands fail to check system keychain for API key
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: 'validateAuthMethod' only checks process.env['GEMINI_API_KEY'] and does not call loadApiKey() from @google/gemini-cli-core to verify the keychain. Non-interactive commands fail with 'When using Gemini API, you must specify the GEMINI_API_KEY environment variable.'

aliases: corrupted settings causes silent backend crash

source_issues.title: [Antigravity] Backend crashes instantly on specific project folders due to corrupted local settings (discoveryMaxDirs: 1e+135)

aliases: duplicate error spam on model switch
remote agent errors repeated per model change
model switch triggers redundant agent refetch
signals.review_reason: Every model switch produces duplicate error spam from remote agent failures, significantly degrading the interactive experience. While not a complete block, the noisy error feedback is a repeated, annoying user-facing degradation that occurs on a common workflow action.

signals.topic: CodeAgent中OpenTelemetry工具span缺少父级ID，破坏trace层级结构导致生产级可观测性失效
signals.summary: CodeAgent使用时会话工具span（如MCPAdaptTool、SimpleTool、FinalAnswerTool）丢失parent关系，被错误标记为根span，打破了正确的trace层级（Agent > Step > LLM > Tool）。受影响版本v1.24.0，而ToolCallingAgent无此问题。用户通过Phoenix/Arize进行生产可观测性监控时，trace链路断裂难以排查问题根因。
signals.review_reason: 这是一个有完整repro和截图证据的真实bug：用户在生产环境中使用Phoenix/Arize进行可观测性监控，CodeAgent的工具span缺少parent导致trace链路断裂，无法追踪工具调用来源，显著影响生产问题排查效率。虽然count=1，但review_reason给出了明确的用户可感知影响（生产可观测性失效），且提供了完整环境信息、依赖版本和对比截图。

source_issues.title: BUG: Missing parent id for OpenTelemetry tool spans when using CodeAgent
source_issues.evidence: 用户通过Phoenix（opentelemetry）进行生产级追踪，工具span（FinalAnswerTool、MCPAdaptTool、SimpleTool）缺少parent，被上升为根span，而正确结构应为Agent > Step > LLM > Tool。提供了完整repro代码和span层级截图对比，v1.24.0引入的回归，ToolCallingAgent无此问题。

signals.topic: Root-only cloud GPU environments (RunPod/Lambda/Vast.ai) block autonomous loop — `--dangerously-skip-permissions` unusable
signals.summary: Claude Code's `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag is blocked when running as root, which is the default on most cloud GPU providers (RunPod, Lambda, Vast.ai). This makes the entire autonomous research loop impossible on the most common ML infrastructure, forcing users into fragile workarounds.
signals.review_reason: This is the primary blocker for the project's core use case. Autoresearch's autonomous loop requires unattended operation, but the `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag is hard-blocked by Claude Code when running as root — the default on all major cloud GPU providers. User spent 16 hours, 88 experiment attempts with only 3 real results. Without a resolution, the main workflow is completely unusable on RunPod/Lambda/Vast.ai, which represent the most common infrastructure for ML research.

source_issues.title: --dangerously-skip-permissions blocked on RunPod (root-only environments)
source_issues.evidence: User spent 16 hours across 3 attempts on H100 80GB trying to run autonomous loop on RunPod. Claude Code blocks --dangerously-skip-permissions under root. Agent stops every 2-3 minutes waiting for human approval, making autonomous operation impossible. Workaround of creating non-root user introduces git ownership conflicts and file permission issues.

signals.topic: BPB evaluation metric silently inflated due to UTF-8 replacement character byte-count bug in prepare.py
signals.summary: The BPB metric — the core evaluation metric driving all experiment decisions — is systematically underestimated because non-UTF-8 BPE tokens are decoded with U+FFFD (3 bytes), inflating the byte-count denominator. This causes experiments to appear better than they are.
aliases: UTF-8 replacement character inflate byte count
signals.review_reason: BPB is the single evaluation metric that drives every decision in the autonomous research loop — which experiments to keep, which to discard, and what to propose next. A systematic underestimation means users may accept models that are not actually better, wasting compute and producing misleading results. This silently corrupts research conclusions without any warning to users.

source_issues.title: Bug: BPB metric inflated by UTF-8 replacement characters in token byte count
source_issues.evidence: In prepare.py lines 188-193, tiktoken.decode() replaces non-UTF-8 continuation bytes with U+FFFD (replacement character), which encodes to 3 bytes instead of 1. This inflates the byte-count denominator in BPB, producing artificially lower (better-looking) scores. Since BPB is the core metric driving the entire autoresearch loop, all experiment comparisons and decisions are corrupted.

signals.topic: Editable install (`uv pip install -e .` / `pip install -e .`) fails due to multiple top-level modules in flat-layout
signals.summary: The project uses a flat Python file layout (train.py, prepare.py at repo root) without a package structure. Both pip and uv refuse editable install with 'Multiple top-level modules discovered in a flat-layout' error, blocking local development and extension.
signals.review_reason: Editable install is the standard workflow for local development and extension of Python projects. Its failure blocks any user who wants to modify, extend, or debug the project locally — a core developer workflow. The error message is opaque to most users and the fix requires packaging knowledge that many researchers lack.

source_issues.title: Editable install fails due to multiple top-level modules (setuptools discovery issue)
source_issues.evidence: Both `uv pip install -e .` and `pip install -e .` fail with error: 'Multiple top-level modules discovered in a flat-layout: [train, prepare]'. Requires manual pyproject.toml modification to add [tool.setuptools] py-modules = ['train', 'prepare']. User on HPC cluster cannot extend or modify project locally without this workaround.

signals.topic: Tokenizer.encode() raises NameError/UnboundLocalError when prepend is a string due to variable scope bug
signals.summary: The prepend_id variable is assigned inside an outer if-block but referenced inside a nested if-block, causing NameError when prepend is a string and encode_single_token() is involved. Additionally, multi-token prepend strings raise ValueError as encode_single_token requires exactly one token.
signals.review_reason: Tokenizer.encode() is called during data preprocessing (prepare.py), which is a prerequisite step before any experiments can run. A NameError or ValueError in this function blocks the entire pipeline. The scope bug also makes the code fragile to future refactoring.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Tokenizer.encode: prepend_id scope issue causes NameError when prepend is string
source_issues.evidence: In Tokenizer.encode(), prepend_id is defined inside `if prepend is not None:` block but used inside nested `if isinstance(text, str):` block. When prepend is a string, encode_single_token() is called which raises ValueError for multi-token strings, and the scope dependency creates fragile behavior. Reproducible with any BOS token string containing multiple BPE tokens.

signals.topic: Eval time caveat undocumented — custom training scripts can cause 20+ minute eval, reducing throughput from ~10 to ~2 experiments/hour
signals.summary: The README advertises '100 experiments while you sleep' based on the built-in eval (~10 sec). When adapting autoresearch to custom training scripts with larger validation sets, eval time can reach 21+ minutes per experiment, making the advertised throughput unrealistic.
signals.review_reason: While documented in a user report, this represents a real expectation mismatch for anyone adapting autoresearch to custom training scripts. Users may plan compute budgets based on misleading throughput estimates. This is user-facing documentation friction with measurable cost implications.

source_issues.title: --dangerously-skip-permissions blocked on RunPod (root-only environments)
source_issues.evidence: User adapting autoresearch for OpenAI parameter-golf contest found sliding window eval on FineWeb validation takes 21 minutes (vs ~10 sec built-in). This changes throughput from ~10 exp/hour to ~2 exp/hour, making the README's '100 experiments while you sleep' estimate fundamentally inaccurate.

signals.topic: RunnableWithFallbacks model parameter breaks agent creation with AttributeError

signals.review_reason: Primary agent creation flow is completely blocked with a reproducible AttributeError when using LangChain's standard .with_fallbacks() pattern. source_issues.evidence: Reproducible AttributeError at resolve_model when passing RunnableWithFallbacks; primary agent creation flow blocked; regression from 0.4.1; includes minimal reproducible example with full stack trace.

source_issues.title: `DaytonaSandbox` hangs on `read()` using custom snapshot image
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible hang when calling read() on DaytonaSandbox with a custom snapshot image; includes reproducible example; marked as bug not feature request.

signals.topic: OpenAI agent factory forces tool_choice="required", breaking all thinking/reasoning models (qwen3.5-plus, deepseek-r1, etc.)
signals.summary: When using ChatOpenAI/init_chat_model with thinking/reasoning models (qwen3.5-plus, deepseek-r1), the agent factory hardcodes tool_choice="required", causing API to return 400 error because thinking models only support "auto" or "none".
aliases: reasoning model agent tool required failure
signals.review_reason: This is a primary workflow blocker. Users building agents with popular thinking/reasoning models (qwen3.5-plus, deepseek-r1) cannot use tool-calling agents at all — every invocation fails with a 400 API error. The root cause is a hardcoded value in the agent factory that has no user-configurable override. Count=1 but this is a clear-cut code defect causing total failure of agent execution with a growing class of models (reasoning/thinking models are increasingly standard).

source_issues.title: openai model: tool_choice="required" not compatible with thinking models (qwen3.5-plus)
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with reproduction steps. When using thinking models (qwen3.5-plus, deepseek-r1) with ChatOpenAI/init_chat_model, the agent factory forces tool_choice="required", causing API 400 error. Thinking models do NOT support tool_choice="required", only "auto" or "none". In langchain/agents/factory.py, _execute_model_sync forces tool_choice="required", which breaks all thinking models.

signals.topic: _consolidate_calls UnboundLocalError crash for unrecognized server tool names (computer, image_generation, etc.)
signals.summary: In langchain-openai _compat.py, _consolidate_calls matches server_tool_call/server_tool_result pairs but has no fallback for unrecognized tool names, leaving the collapsed variable unassigned and crashing with UnboundLocalError.
signals.review_reason: UnboundLocalError is a hard crash that completely blocks the Responses API workflow for any user employing server tools not in the allowlist (computer tool, image_generation, etc.). Every invocation with an unrecognized tool name crashes immediately with no workaround. The code has an obvious missing code path (no else/fallback branch) making this a clear code defect.

source_issues.title: langchain-openai: _consolidate_calls raises UnboundLocalError for unrecognized server tool names
source_issues.evidence: Bug with reproducible code snippet. _consolidate_calls in _compat.py handles web_search, file_search, code_interpreter, remote_mcp, mcp_list_tools by name, but if the tool name doesn't match (e.g. computer, image_generation), collapsed is never assigned and yield collapsed raises UnboundLocalError. Reproduction: passing items with type server_tool_call and name 'computer' causes immediate crash.

signals.topic: HuggingFaceEmbeddings performance: per-batch device-to-CPU transfers cause ~1.84x slowdown on MPS/CUDA
signals.summary: HuggingFaceEmbeddings._embed defaults to convert_to_numpy=True, causing a device-to-CPU synchronization point inside every micro-batch loop instead of once at the end, adding ~640ms overhead on M4 MacBook Air for 1000 texts. Combined with Chroma.from_texts re-embedding per storage batch, users experience significant cost and time loss.
aliases: Chroma from_texts re-embeds per batch performance
signals.review_reason: This causes measurable cost and time loss in embedding-heavy pipelines (RAG, Chroma indexing). The default behavior makes HuggingFaceEmbeddings ~1.84x slower than necessary on every batch, directly wasting GPU/MPS compute and developer time. The issue includes reproducible benchmarks and identifies both the root cause in HuggingFaceEmbeddings._embed and a secondary issue in Chroma.from_texts.

source_issues.title: perf: HuggingFaceEmbeddings causes excessive device-to-cpu transfers per batch
source_issues.evidence: Performance bug with benchmark evidence. Default convert_to_numpy=True in sentence_transformers.encode() calls .cpu().float().numpy() inside every micro-batch iteration. On MPS/CUDA each .cpu() is a full synchronization point. For 1000 texts at batch_size=32, this means 32 synchronisations instead of 1, adding ~640ms overhead. Benchmark shows 1.84x speedup with fix (0.631s vs 1.157s). Also Chroma.from_texts re-embeds per storage batch.
