signals.topic: AsyncPregelLoop replay/interrupt time-travel bug — interrupts fail during replay
signals.summary: 在 replay 模式下恢复被中断的状态时，interrupt 机制无法正常工作，导致 replay 流程被阻断。
signals.review_reason: 两条 issue 均指向 AsyncPregelLoop 异步循环核心逻辑故障：issue #7256 由维护者提交，关联 PR #7225，说明是确认的主流程阻断 bug；issue #6950 是已加 bug 标签的生产环境随机 CancelledError，导致异步清理阶段抛出未捕获异常。两者共同指向 AsyncPregelLoop 的 replay/interrupt/cleanup 核心路径不可靠，为典型主流程阻断问题，且 count=2 有具体样例支撑。

source_issues.title: time travel bug -- resuming interrupts on "replay"
source_issues.evidence: 用户在 replay 场景下恢复 interrupt 时行为不正确，langgraph 维护者确认并关联 PR #7225。

source_issues.title: Random CancelledError in AsyncPregelLoop cleanup
source_issues.evidence: AsyncPregelLoop.__aexit__ 中抛出 asyncio.CancelledError，在 LangSmith Cloud 生产环境中随机出现，stack trace 明确指向 AsyncPregelLoop 异步清理流程崩溃。

signals.topic: Run cancellation causes in-progress streamed state to be lost — checkpoints not persisted on abort
signals.summary: 用户取消运行或断开流连接时，已流式输出但尚未 checkpoint 持久化的状态全部丢失，前端重同步后用户可见内容消失。
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1，但用户影响极为明确：取消运行导致用户在界面上已看到的流式输出数据永久丢失，破坏了'所见即保存'的会话连续性，对聊天和实时 UI 应用构成显著体验下降和潜在数据损失，是明确的用户可感知痛点。

source_issues.title: Run Cancellation Causes Loss of Streamed State Not Yet Persisted as a Checkpoint
source_issues.evidence: 用户在取消运行后，已流式输出的数据在重新同步 UI 时全部丢失，backend 仅反映最近一次 checkpoint 的状态。作者明确描述'用户可以看到几秒钟的输出，但取消并发送新消息后输出消失'，并指出 checkpoint 仅在任务完成时持久化，取消时无 flush 机制。

signals.topic: get_subgraph() logic bug when node names share a common prefix — returns wrong subgraph
signals.summary: 当父图中存在共享前缀的多个子图节点时，get_subgraphs() 使用 startswith 匹配导致算法错误匹配并返回错误的子图，使生产环境中图遍历逻辑静默失败。
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1，但这是生产环境中已确认的逻辑 bug：当子图节点名称互为前缀时 get_subgraphs() 返回错误结果，导致图遍历静默失败。影响 subgraph 调试、嵌套图遍历等关键功能，属于关键功能不可用的边缘场景，且有可复现代码支撑。

source_issues.title: get_subgraph fails when nodes share a common prefix
source_issues.evidence: 作者在生产环境中触发了此 bug：两个节点名称有共同前缀且均包含子图时，get_subgraphs() 错误匹配并返回错误的子图，导致图遍历静默失败。作者提供了可运行的最小复现示例，assertion 在示例末尾失败，并提交了 PR #6366 修复。

signals.topic: AsyncPostgresStore.abatch double connection checkout — redundant connections acquired and wasted
signals.summary: abatch 方法先获取一个连接但未实际使用，又在 _cursor 中再次获取连接执行查询，导致使用 AsyncConnectionPool 时每次 abatch 调用从池中双重检出连接，浪费资源。
signals.review_reason: AsyncPostgresStore.abatch 连接双重检出 bug 存在明确的技术证据，消耗连接池资源造成浪费，在高并发场景下可能耗尽连接池。但无主流程阻断，且 issue 中未见用户描述由此引发的实际生产故障，故归为 P2 资源效率问题。

source_issues.title: AsyncPostgresStore.abatch acquires unused connection and double-checks out from pool
source_issues.evidence: AsyncPostgresStore.abatch 调用 _ainternal.get_connection() 获取连接但未使用，_execute_batch 内部 _cursor(pipeline=True) 再执行一次 get_connection() 进行真实查询，导致一个 abatch 调用从池中双重检出两个连接，仅一个用于实际工作。

signals.topic: iPhone 12/13 Safari: chat message text not displayed — only empty bubble container renders
signals.summary: On iPhone 12 and iPhone 13 devices (Safari and WeChat in-app browser), chat message text inside bubbles is invisible/blank. Both user messages and AI replies are affected. Appears related to iOS WebKit Markdown/Streamdown rendering.
aliases: chat bubble text missing on iPhone
signals.review_reason: User-facing UI bug that renders chat completely unusable on a specific device family (iPhone 12/13). Affects both sending and receiving messages, confirmed reproducible. Not P0 because count=1 and no other users reported the same issue.

source_issues.title: On iPhone 12 and iPhone 13, chat messages only show the bubble container, while the actual message text is not displayed.
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug on iPhone 12/13 (Safari + WeChat in-app browser). Both user and AI message text are invisible inside bubbles. Issue is reproducible, user attempted multiple fixes without success. Does not affect iPhone 15 Pro. Root cause likely in Markdown/Streamdown rendering path under iOS WebKit.

signals.topic: LEGACY userinput.files field blocks all downstream Agent nodes in Workflow apps
signals.summary: Workflow-type apps automatically generate a system-level LEGACY userinput.files field that cannot be removed via UI. This field causes every downstream Agent node to fail with 'file type parameter file not supported in agent', even when Agent nodes don't reference it. No workaround exists.
aliases: workflow agent node file parameter error
signals.review_reason: Complete workflow blocking bug. All Agent nodes in Workflow-type apps fail unconditionally because of an auto-generated field that cannot be removed or disabled. No workaround exists. This is a high-impact, high-confidence user pain point.

source_issues.title: Cannot remove userinput.files LEGACY field from Workflow app — causes Agent node failures
source_issues.evidence: System-generated LEGACY field cannot be deleted via UI. Every downstream Agent node fails with 'file type parameter file not supported in agent'. No workaround: no delete option in UI, no Features toggle for Workflow-type apps, duplication carries field over. Blocks all Agent-based Workflow apps entirely.

signals.topic: Docker Compose startup fails: service definitions (seekdb, db_mysql, oceanbase) not found
signals.summary: Users deploying Dify via Docker Compose encounter 'no such service' errors for multiple database services (seekdb, db_mysql, oceanbase). docker-compose up -d repeatedly fails with no working path forward.
signals.review_reason: Complete deployment blocking bug. Dify cannot be started via Docker Compose, making the entire platform inaccessible. No workaround described. Despite count=1, this is an absolute blocker for all self-hosted deployments encountering this service definition mismatch.

source_issues.title: docker compose start failed
source_issues.evidence: User reports 'no such service: seekdb', 'no such service: db_mysql', 'no such service: oceanbase' on repeated docker-compose up -d attempts. Confirmed using Docker Compose v2.20.0. System completely fails to start.

signals.topic: Dify login page returns 502 Bad Gateway — system inaccessible
signals.summary: Dify login page fails with 502 Bad Gateway error. Backend returns HTML instead of JSON, causing SyntaxError. Users cannot access the Dify system at all.
signals.review_reason: Absolute access blocker. User cannot even reach the Dify login page. This is a complete system inaccessibility issue, which is the highest severity for a user pain point.

source_issues.title: dify系统进不去3323
source_issues.evidence: Login page fails with 502 Bad Gateway. Uncaught SyntaxError: 'Unexpected token <, <html> is not valid JSON' indicates nginx/proxy is returning an error page instead of backend JSON. User cannot access Dify at all.

signals.topic: OpenAI LLM node JSON/structured output mode broken — regression
signals.summary: Using response_format=json or structured output in OpenAI LLM node throws 'Responses.create() got an unexpected keyword argument response_format'. Same feature works correctly with Gemini. Affects OpenAI Responses API users.
signals.review_reason: Regression that breaks JSON structured output for OpenAI models — a key feature for LLM-driven workflows. Explicitly marked as regression. Not P0 because count=1 and OpenAI Responses API configuration may be non-default.

source_issues.title: OpenAI Response Mode json failure (works with Gemini but not in OpenAI models) - regression
source_issues.evidence: PluginInvokeError: Responses.create() got an unexpected keyword argument 'response_format'. Works with Gemini LLM node. User is using Responses API=true in OpenAI credentials. Explicitly marked as regression, meaning previously-working functionality is now broken.

signals.topic: Qdrant local storage silently deletes all data on process restart due to on_disk default being False
signals.summary: When using Qdrant with local path storage, shutil.rmtree() is unconditionally called on every init when on_disk=False (the default), silently destroying all persisted data. Users lose all memory data after every program restart with no warning.
aliases: Qdrant on_disk default causes data deletion
shutil.rmtree called on Qdrant local path initialization
signals.review_reason: Direct user data loss with every restart. No warning, no error message — data is silently wiped. This is a P0 data-loss bug that permanently destroys user memories. Count=1 (single issue), but the severity of silent unconditional data deletion warrants P0 priority with explicit user-impact evidence.

source_issues.title: Bug Report: Qdrant Local Storage Loses Data on Restart Due to on_disk Default
source_issues.evidence: shutil.rmtree(path) unconditionally called on every init when on_disk is False (default), silently deleting all persisted data. No warning to user. User loses all memory after every restart.

signals.topic: Valkey vector store corrupts embeddings when update() is called with vector=None, permanently making memories unsearchable
signals.summary: When Memory._add_to_vector_store() detects unchanged content (NONE event) and calls vector_store.update() with vector=None, Valkey's update() unconditionally serializes None via np.array(None, dtype=np.float32), overwriting the correct embedding with 4 bytes of garbage. Memory becomes permanently unsearchable via vector similarity.
aliases: Valkey embedding corruption on unchanged memory update
memory becomes unsearchable after update with vector=None
signals.review_reason: Permanent, silent data corruption: embeddings overwritten with garbage, making memories permanently unsearchable. Triggered by a routine memory update — not an edge case. The corrupted memories cannot be recovered without re-embedding all content. P0 severity despite count=1.

source_issues.title: Mem0 with Valkey: update() corrupts embeddings when called with vector=None
source_issues.evidence: np.array(None, dtype=np.float32).tobytes() writes 4 bytes of garbage over correct embedding. Memory text content intact but permanently unsearchable via vector similarity. Caused by routine update() call when content is unchanged.

signals.topic: OpenClaw plugin: pg CommonJS import fails at runtime causing memory_store and memory_search to break
signals.summary: In the bundled mem0ai OSS build, 'pg' is imported with named exports (import { Client } from 'pg'), which fails at runtime when pg resolves as CommonJS in the OpenClaw plugin environment. This breaks memory_store and memory_search for all OpenClaw plugin users, requiring manual patch of built files.
aliases: pg named export error in OpenClaw
CommonJS pg import fails in bundled mem0ai
memory tools broken in OpenClaw plugin environment
signals.review_reason: Runtime crash that blocks core memory operations (store, search, get, forget) for all OpenClaw plugin users. Main flow completely broken. Count=1 but clear user impact: the entire memory toolchain is non-functional requiring manual binary patching as workaround.

source_issues.title: openclaw-mem0: memory_store/search fail with pg CommonJS import (Named export 'Client' not found)
source_issues.evidence: SyntaxError: Named export 'Client' not found. The requested module 'pg' is a CommonJS module. Breaks memory_store and memory_search in real OpenClaw runtime. Workaround requires manually patching built file.

signals.topic: MCP search_memory operator precedence bug causes TypeError crash when accessible_memory_ids is empty/None
signals.summary: In openmemory/api/app/mcp_server.py, the condition 'if allowed and h.id is None or h.id not in allowed' has incorrect operator precedence parsed as '(allowed and h.id is None) or (h.id not in allowed)'. When accessible_memory_ids is None, this causes 'TypeError: argument of type NoneType is not iterable' and crashes search functionality.
aliases: MCP search_memory TypeError NoneType not iterable
signals.review_reason: Runtime TypeError crash that completely breaks MCP search_memory. Clear user impact with a reproducible crash path. Count=1 but this is a straightforward coding bug causing total failure of search functionality.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Operator precedence error in mcp_server.py search_memory function causes TypeError when filtering memories
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable at mcp_server.py:218. Root cause: missing parentheses in boolean expression causing incorrect operator precedence. Search crashes for any user with empty/None accessible_memory_ids.

signals.topic: MCP add_memories tool blocks synchronously for 2+ minutes, blocking MCP clients like Claude Code
signals.summary: The add_memories MCP tool in OpenMemory processes everything inline — embedding generation, vector store writes, Neo4j graph updates, and database logging — causing the MCP client to block for over 2 minutes on a single call. Any client using this tool (e.g., Claude Code) becomes unresponsive during this time.
aliases: OpenMemory MCP synchronous processing blocks client
MCP client timeout due to synchronous memory operations
signals.review_reason: Main workflow completely blocked for 2+ minutes per add_memories call. MCP client becomes unresponsive. This is a workflow-blocking issue that makes the tool effectively unusable in real production scenarios. User measured 2m19s blocking time.

source_issues.title: OpenMemory MCP add_memories tool blocks synchronously for 2+ minutes
source_issues.evidence: Single add_memories call took 2 minutes 19 seconds. MCP client (Claude Code) blocked for entire duration. Embedding, vector writes, graph updates, and DB logging all happen inline synchronously.

signals.topic: UseAIContextProviders accumulates AIContext tools in ChatOptions across repeated calls, causing API 400 rejection on Anthropic
signals.summary: UseAIContextProviders merges AIContext.Tools into ChatOptions.Tools on every API call without deduplication. When ChatOptions.Tools is a shared mutable list reference, tools accumulate multiplicatively. Anthropic API rejects with HTTP 400 'Tool names must be unique', blocking the primary agent call path for Anthropic users.
signals.review_reason: Primary agent flow fails with HTTP 400 for Anthropic users after just 2 calls due to tool accumulation. Count=1 because only one issue in this file, but user impact is severe: API-level blocking requiring a non-obvious pipeline workaround. Not P0 because only one affected repo and count < 3.

source_issues.title: .NET: UseAIContextProviders accumulates context provider tools in ChatOptions.Tools across calls
source_issues.evidence: API rejects with HTTP 400 'Tool names must be unique.' on Anthropic after second call. Tool list grows unboundedly across calls, wasting tokens. Workaround required in DelegatingChatClient to reset list before each call.

signals.topic: AzureAIClient observability produces fragmented trace IDs, breaking end-to-end tracing in Azure AI Foundry
signals.summary: Single logical agent run is split into multiple unrelated trace IDs in Azure AI Foundry. Each Responses API call appears as an independent trace, making observability effectively unusable. Root cause: configure_azure_monitor() does not instrument the httpx transport used internally by the OpenAI Python SDK.
signals.review_reason: Key observability feature is broken for the default non-streaming Azure AI path. Users cannot debug multi-step agent runs in Azure AI Foundry, forcing manual instrumentation workarounds. Count=1 and single repo, but user impact is significant: critical debugging capability unavailable by default in production path.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: AzureAIClient.configure_azure_monitor does not preserve a single Foundry trace
source_issues.evidence: A single agent run produces multiple unrelated trace IDs. Debugging a run across multiple model calls is impossible. Requires manual HTTPXClientInstrumentor workaround. Streaming has a separate root cause.

signals.topic: AG-UI streaming reasoning content disappears from MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT after stream completes
signals.summary: During streaming, AG-UI correctly emits REASONING_START/MESSAGE_CONTENT/END events. After the run finishes, the final MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT omits all reasoning content. Frontends that rely on MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT as the source of truth lose all reasoning data immediately upon stream completion.
signals.review_reason: Reasoning display works during streaming but silently disappears in the final snapshot that frontends use as source of truth. This breaks any CopilotKit or similar frontend that relies on MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT. User-reported as blocking for a production frontend integration.

source_issues.title: Python: agent-framework-ag-ui: include reasoning messages in MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT
source_issues.evidence: Frontend using CopilotKit shows reasoning during streaming but loses all of it when stream ends and MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT is received. _emit_text_reasoning() does not persist to FlowState. _build_messages_snapshot() has no reasoning branch.

signals.topic: Hosted MCP sample fails at runtime due to AzureOpenAIChatClient sending unsupported 'mcp' tool type to API
signals.summary: The agent_with_hosted_mcp sample fails with HTTP 400 'Invalid value: mcp. Supported values are: function and custom.' AzureOpenAIChatClient passes the MCP tool spec with type='mcp' directly to the Azure OpenAI API without translating it, causing the sample to fail on first use.
aliases: MCP tool type not supported by Azure OpenAI
signals.review_reason: The official hosted MCP sample is broken at runtime for all users trying it on Azure OpenAI. New users hit an immediate 400 error on first use, blocking onboarding. Sample is part of the v1.0 release. Not P0 because count=1 and single repo, but impact is high: official sample completely unusable.

source_issues.title: Python: agent_with_hosted_mcp sample fails - AzureOpenAIChatClient sends unsupported mcp tool type to API
source_issues.evidence: Sample fails with 400 error immediately on first request. Root cause is direct pass-through of MCP tool config without translation. Found during V1.0 bug bash.

signals.topic: Workflow executors cannot access /responses request metadata or AgentMiddleware context, breaking standard auth patterns
signals.summary: AgentMiddleware provides request context (e.g. headers) to agents via context.agent._request_headers, but this mechanism does not work in Workflow executors. FunctionMiddleware receives empty kwargs. Users building production workflows with authentication tokens cannot access request context in their executor logic.
signals.review_reason: Standard authentication and context-forwarding patterns that work in regular agents completely break in Workflows. Users cannot build production workflows with per-request auth. This is a key functional gap between agent and workflow usage modes.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Unable to access /responses metadata field in Agent Framework Workflows
source_issues.evidence: Metadata passed in /responses API call is inaccessible in Workflow Executor. AgentMiddleware works for regular agents but FunctionMiddleware gets empty kwargs in Workflow context. Users cannot forward auth tokens to tools.

signals.topic: MCP tool poisoning enables arbitrary code execution via unverified tool definitions
signals.summary: AutoGen's MCP integration trusts tool definitions fetched via session.list_tools() without signature verification or schema pinning. Malicious MCP servers can inject instructions via tool descriptions, change schemas between sessions, or modify parameters in transit, creating a path from tool poisoning to arbitrary code execution including ransomware and data exfiltration.
aliases: MCP tool poisoning arbitrary code execution
signals.review_reason: Security vulnerability with concrete evidence: CVSS 9.6 CVE, 437K+ affected downloads, active malicious MCP server found in the wild, and 72.8% poisoning success rate in published research. MCP integration is a core feature path. Despite being reported via a GitHub issue (not a dedicated CVE disclosure), the user impact evidence is explicit and severe — arbitrary code execution including ransomware delivery and data exfiltration. The 'only connect to trusted servers' warning is acknowledged as insufficient by the reporter and relates to guardrails epic #6017 and #7266.

source_issues.title: MCP tool poisoning can enable arbitrary code execution via unsigned tool definitions
source_issues.evidence: Cited research: 72.8% tool poisoning success rate across 20 LLM agents (MCPTox, arXiv:2508.14925). CVE-2025-6514 (CVSS 9.6) affecting mcp-remote RCE with 437K+ downloads. postmark-mcp malicious MCP server found in the wild with 1,643 downloads. The only mitigation is an insufficient docstring warning 'Only connect to trusted MCP servers.' The description field flows directly to the LLM agent with code execution tools available.

signals.topic: JupyterCodeExecutor leaks temporary output directory on stop(), unlike all other executors
signals.summary: JupyterCodeExecutor creates a temp directory via tempfile.mkdtemp() when no output_dir is provided, but never cleans it up in stop(). Other executors (LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor, DockerCommandLineCodeExecutor, AzureContainerCodeExecutor) all properly clean up. Over many executor lifecycles, leaked directories and their contents (images, HTML files) accumulate on disk.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug with provided PoC. The JupyterCodeExecutor fails to clean up temp directories created via tempfile.mkdtemp() on stop(), unlike every other executor in the codebase. This causes resource leakage (accumulating directories and files) on disk over time. The class even has a declared _temp_dir field suggesting the auto-cleanup pattern was intended but not implemented. Reproducible with the included PoC.

source_issues.title: JupyterCodeExecutor leaks temporary output directory on stop — inconsistent with other executors
source_issues.evidence: PoC provided: creating 3 JupyterCodeExecutor instances without output_dir, calling start/execute/stop, then verifying all 3 temp directories still exist after stop(). Also: class declares self._temp_dir: Optional[tempfile.TemporaryDirectory[str]] = None on line 151, suggesting the intention was to use TemporaryDirectory() for auto-cleanup but it was never used. Inconsistency with all other executors that properly clean up.

signals.topic: CodeExecutorAgent polymorphism broken: classmethod called via concrete class breaks subclass overrides
signals.summary: In CodeExecutorAgent.on_messages_stream, the class method _reflect_on_code_block_results_flow is invoked via the concrete class name instead of using self or a method that supports polymorphism. This breaks subclass overrides of _reflect_on_code_block_results_flow. This is the same root cause as issue #5953, indicating a recurring pattern in the codebase.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug preventing extensibility of CodeExecutorAgent via subclassing. The static binding to the concrete class name means custom subclass implementations of _reflect_on_code_block_results_flow are silently ignored, breaking expected Python polymorphism behavior. Has a prior occurrence (#5953) indicating a systemic pattern issue. Impact is real for users trying to customize agent behavior, though it does not block the default main flow.

source_issues.title: Polymorphism issue: CodeExecutorAgent calls classmethod via concrete class in on_messages_stream
source_issues.evidence: Reporter shows that creating a child class of CodeExecutorAgent and overriding _reflect_on_code_block_results_flow still results in parent class methods being called. References same root cause as issue #5953, indicating a recurring pattern. Code reference points to line 667-675 in _code_executor_agent.py where static binding to CodeExecutorAgent is introduced.

signals.topic: schema_to_pydantic_model loses $defs type information (array becomes object)
signals.summary: When converting a JSON schema generated by Pydantic v2 using schema_to_pydantic_model, type information inside $defs is not preserved. Specifically, array types become empty objects, losing the 'type: array' and 'items' structure. This breaks schemas with type aliases like list[str] defined in Pydantic models.
aliases: Pydantic v2 schema conversion array type bug
signals.review_reason: Confirmed data corruption bug in a core utility (schema_to_pydantic_model) with provided PoC. Type aliases in Pydantic v2 schemas have their array type information silently converted to empty objects, breaking the generated model schema. This affects any workflow that uses schema_to_pydantic_model for tool schema generation with type-aliased fields. Non-blocking but clearly a functional defect with reproducible impact.

source_issues.title: schema_to_pydantic_model loses $defs type information (array → object)
source_issues.evidence: Repro case provided: Pydantic model with type alias TaskData = list[str] generates $defs.TaskData with type: array and items: {type: string}. After schema_to_pydantic_model, $defs.TaskData becomes {properties: {}, type: object} — the array structure is destroyed. This is a data corruption bug in a core utility used for tool schema generation.

signals.topic: AutoGen agents blocked from web research on Cloudflare-protected sites (403 errors)
signals.summary: AutoGen agents performing web research encounter 403 errors on Cloudflare-protected sites, which make up ~60% of high-value web targets (news, LinkedIn, Amazon, government sites). Standard HTTP fetchers fail on these sites, preventing agents from completing research tasks.
aliases: Cloudflare bypass blocked for AutoGen agents
403 errors on web scraping research tasks
signals.review_reason: User-reported functional limitation: AutoGen agents are blocked from web research on ~60% of high-value web targets due to Cloudflare bot protection returning 403 errors. The reporter is an affected user (not a tool vendor), and 3 comments indicate community interest. However, the issue is framed as a tool suggestion rather than a bug report, and the proposed solution involves a third-party MCP server, suggesting this may be an ecosystem limitation rather than a framework bug. Marked P2 and lower confidence due to the feature-request framing.

source_issues.title: Tool suggestion: anybrowse for MCP-native web scraping with Cloudflare bypass
source_issues.evidence: Reporter explicitly states: 'AutoGen agents doing web research hit a common wall: Cloudflare-protected sites return 403s or empty content. Standard HTTP fetchers don't work on ~60% of high-value web targets.' User evidence: 3 comments on the issue indicating community interest. The reporter is proposing a specific MCP solution (anybrowse) but the underlying problem of 403 failures blocking research agents is user-reported.

signals.topic: response.body() returns mojibake (double-encoded UTF-8) for SSE streaming responses
signals.summary: When consuming SSE (Server-Sent Events) responses, response.body() returns double-encoded UTF-8 bytes producing garbled text (mojibake), while route.fetch() returns correct bytes. Affects Chinese text and other non-ASCII content in SSE streams.
aliases: SSE streaming response body encoding bug
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues (open + closed) confirm this bug. response.body() silently returns garbled data for SSE responses with non-ASCII content. route.fetch() works correctly, showing this is Playwright-specific. Affects real-world SSE use cases (live data feeds, chat, notifications) for international users. Cross-platform (Windows confirmed). Count=2 meets P0 threshold but the bug is not a primary flow blocker — it corrupts data rather than blocking execution.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: response.body() returns mojibake (double-encoded UTF-8) for SSE streaming responses
source_issues.evidence: Full repro with server.ts and client.ts. response.body() returns \xc3\xa4\xc2\xbd\xc2\xa0 (double-encoded) instead of \xe4\xbd\xa0 (correct). route.fetch() returns correct bytes. CDP Network.getResponseBody also shows the bug.

source_issues.title: response.body() returns mojibake (double-encoded UTF-8) for SSE streaming responses
source_issues.evidence: Same bug confirmed in playwright-python and playwright-dotnet. Original report via playwright-python issue #3023. Windows user confirmed.

signals.topic: --last-failed silently drops all tests when config uses project dependencies (returns 'No tests found')
signals.summary: Using --last-failed flag with Playwright configs that have project dependencies results in 'Error: No tests found' even when .last-run.json contains valid failed test IDs. The postShardTestFilters run before dependency projects are added to rootSuite, so failed tests from dependency projects are never matched.
aliases: last-failed filter skips dependency project tests
signals.review_reason: Primary flow blocker: --last-failed is a core CI/CD feature that silently breaks when using project dependencies, the most common real-world Playwright config pattern. Error is silent (no helpful message), primary use case (rerunning failed tests in dependency setups) is completely broken. Root cause is precisely identified. Count=2 with strong instrumentation evidence. P0 warranted.

source_issues.title: [BUG]: --last-failed silently drops all tests when using project dependencies
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in runner/loadUtils.js lines 173-174: postShardTestFilters runs before dependency projects are added. Failed test IDs from 'default' project don't match 'sequential' project test IDs → all sequential tests filtered out → 'No tests found'. Confirmed via instrumentation showing failedTestIds from 'default' never seen by filter.

signals.topic: macOS: Playwright-launched browser windows cannot receive physical keyboard input
signals.summary: On macOS, browsers launched via childProcess.spawn() are not registered with WindowServer, causing physical keyboard events to be silently dropped regardless of visual focus. Affects MCP automation tools, semi-automated testing, and debugging workflows.
aliases: keyboard input not delivered to browser
signals.review_reason: Root cause is clearly identified: childProcess.spawn() bypasses macOS Launch Services so the browser is never registered with WindowServer. This blocks real workflows (MCP tools, debugging, manual testing). Verified by comparing spawn() vs open -na behavior. Not P0 because count=1 and affects only macOS non-headless users.

source_issues.title: macOS: Browser window cannot receive keyboard focus when launched via childProcess.spawn()
source_issues.evidence: Browser is visible and clickable via CDP but physical keystrokes go to previously focused app. lsappinfo shows [NULL]. Process parent chain is Chrome→node→npm instead of Chrome→launchd.

signals.topic: VS Code extension embedded trace viewer blank in Playwright 1.58.0 (regression from 1.57)
signals.summary: Embedded trace viewer in Playwright Test for VS Code extension shows nothing after upgrading to 1.58.0. Traces are recorded correctly (trace.zip files exist) and standalone show-trace works. Regression introduced in 1.58.
aliases: trace viewer blank vscode extension 1.58.0 regression
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression: 1.57 works, 1.58 breaks. Trace data is valid but the embedded viewer can't display it. Key debugging feature is broken for VS Code/Cursor users after upgrade. Count=1 so P0 is not warranted, but this is a clear regression affecting a core Playwright debugging workflow.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Embedded trace viewer in VS Code extension shows nothing with Playwright 1.58.0 (works with 1.57.0)
source_issues.evidence: Traces ARE being recorded (valid trace.zip in test-results/). Standalone npx playwright show-trace works. Downgrading to 1.57.0 fixes it. Reproduces with extension 1.1.15 and 1.1.17 on Cursor/macOS.

signals.topic: page.clock.install() breaks performance.measure() returning undefined (TypeError)
signals.summary: Installing page.clock causes performance.measure() to return undefined instead of a PerformanceMeasure object, throwing TypeError when accessing .duration. Affects all browsers (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit).
signals.review_reason: Direct user-impacting bug: tests fail with TypeError because performance.measure() returns undefined after clock.install(). This is a core API regression that breaks any test relying on the Performance API alongside fake timers. Multi-browser impact (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit). Likely SinonJS upstream bug already documented, but Playwright's implementation needs fixing.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: performance.measure returns undefined when installing the page.clock
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'duration') when calling performance.measure() after page.clock.install(). Test fails on Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. Without clock.install() the test passes. Links to similar SinonJS bug.

signals.topic: MCP tool integration trusts server-supplied definitions without integrity verification
signals.summary: MCPPluginBase.load_tools() accepts tool definitions from MCP server without any integrity check. Combined with FunctionChoiceBehavior.Auto(), this creates a tool poisoning attack surface (OWASP MCP-01). Compromised server can inject instructions in tool descriptions, silently reload tool definitions, and pass unsanitised systemPrompt to LLM. Research shows 72.8% attack success rate across 20 LLM agents. CVE-2025-6514 (CVSS 9.6), CVE-2025-49596 (CVSS 9.4) referenced. If agent connects to compromised MCP server with auto-invocation, direct path from tool poisoning to arbitrary code execution exists.
signals.review_reason: MCP工具集成在启用auto-invocation时直接将MCP服务器提供的工具定义注入LLM上下文，无完整性校验。工具描述可被恶意服务器篡改注入指令，工具定义可在用户不知情时动态替换。72.8%攻击成功率，CVE CVSS 9.6/9.4，工具投毒到代码执行的路径直接且无门槛。这是典型的安全+主流程阻断组合，auto function invocation使攻击无需用户交互即可触发。用户在使用MCP插件时面临直接的任意代码执行风险，P0合理。

source_issues.title: MCP tool integration trusts server-supplied definitions without integrity verification
source_issues.evidence: MCP tools loaded via MCPPluginBase.load_tools() accept tool names, descriptions, and parameter schemas directly from MCP server with no integrity check. Combined with FunctionChoiceBehavior.Auto(), creates tool poisoning attack surface. Tool descriptions injected into LLM context unsanitised. message_handler silently reloads tools on notifications/tools/list_changed. Sampling callback passes server-supplied systemPrompt directly to LLM. 72.8% attack success rate (MCPTox benchmark, arXiv:2508.14925). CVE-2025-6514 (CVSS 9.6), CVE-2025-49596 (CVSS 9.4).

signals.topic: Npgsql 10.x incompatibility causes MissingMethodException at runtime in PgVector connector
signals.summary: Using Npgsql 10.0.2 with Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.PgVector throws MissingMethodException on CollectionExistsAsync() call. The ReloadTypesAsync() method signature changed in Npgsql 10.x, breaking runtime compatibility. Combining Entity Framework with PgVector extension triggers this conflict. PgVector auto-installs Npgsql 8.0.7 which works, but upgrading to 10.0.2 causes crash.
signals.review_reason: Npgsql 10.x与PgVector连接器不兼容，在调用CollectionExistsAsync()时抛出MissingMethodException。这是向量数据库核心操作之一，直接阻断检索流程。用户实际场景中（Entity Framework + PgVector）会触发该问题。count=1但影响明确为运行时崩溃+主流程阻断，P0严格按count>=3规则降为P1，需等待同主题issue复现以升级。

source_issues.title: Bug: System.MissingMethodException: 'Method not found: 'System.Threading.Tasks.Task Npgsql.NpgsqlConnection.ReloadTypesAsync()'.'
source_issues.evidence: Using Npgsql 10.0.2 with Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Connectors.PgVector throws MissingMethodException at CollectionExistsAsync(). ReloadTypesAsync() method not found. Issue manifests when combining Entity Framework (which upgrades Npgsql to 10.x) with PgVector connector.

signals.topic: C# nullable plugin parameters generate incorrect JSON schema under AllowStrictSchemaAdherence
signals.summary: In projects with Nullable enable, when using AllowStrictSchemaAdherence, nullable parameters (e.g., string? something) generate schema type: 'string' instead of type: ['string', 'null']. This forces LLM to generate fake data instead of null values, causing data corruption (LLM generates string containing literal 'null' instead of null). Issue only affects direct nullable parameters, not nullable properties in objects.
signals.review_reason: AllowStrictSchemaAdherence模式下，nullable参数生成错误的JSON schema，导致LLM无法正确生成null值而生成伪数据（literal 'null'字符串）。这直接影响工具调用数据正确性，是agent工具调用链路上的关键功能缺陷。用户报告LLM生成的数据损坏（字符串'null'而非null值），影响依赖精确参数的后端逻辑。count=1但影响明确，P1。

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: .Net plugin parameters with AllowStrictSchemaAdherence does not follow nullable
source_issues.evidence: string? parameters generate type: 'string' instead of ['string', 'null'] under AllowStrictSchemaAdherence. LLM generates fake null data (string containing literal 'null') instead of null. Issue reproducible in nullable-enabled C# projects. Works correctly for nullable properties in object parameters but not direct nullable parameters.

signals.topic: Multi-agent GroupChat loses function call results when auto-function invocation is terminated early
signals.summary: When using early termination filter to stop function calls after getting tool result, the terminating agent's response in chat history becomes an empty list ('[]'). The tool result is not used as the agent's response and is invisible to subsequent agents in the group chat. This forces the LLM to make a 3rd unnecessary call just to surface the tool result, wasting tokens and latency.
aliases: GroupChat early termination function result loss
ChatCompletionAgent terminate function call empty response
signals.review_reason: 多agent协作中，早期终止过滤器导致agent响应丢失工具结果，chat history中显示为空列表。后续agent无法访问工具结果，导致不得不额外调用LLM来暴露工具结果，造成显著的token和时间成本。这是multi-agent场景下的关键状态丢失问题，直接影响协作效率和成本。count=1但体验下降和成本损失明确，P1。

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: when terminate a function(tool) call in an Agent, the Groupchat cannot catch functioncallresult in chathistory
source_issues.evidence: Early termination filter context.terminate=True after tool result causes agent A's response in chat history to be '[]' (empty list). Next agent B cannot see tool result. Workaround requires a 3rd LLM call just to surface the tool result, costing significant tokens and latency. User explicitly wants tool result as agent response without extra LLM call.

signals.topic: Process Framework crashes with Circular Reference Error when OpenTelemetry sensitive diagnostics enabled
signals.summary: When running Process Framework samples with SEMANTICKERNEL_EXPERIMENTAL_GENAI_ENABLE_OTEL_DIAGNOSTICS_SENSITIVE=true, every function invocation within a KernelProcessStep fails with 'Circular reference detected' error. The KernelProcessStepContext object passed to step functions contains reference loops that prevent JSON serialization required for sensitive OTel diagnostics. The issue is fundamental to how Kernel.invoke handles KernelProcessStepContext during serialization.
signals.review_reason: 启用OpenTelemetry敏感诊断选项后，Process Framework所有函数调用均因循环引用而崩溃。这直接阻断用户在生产环境中使用诊断工具进行调试和可观测性建设。虽然是实验性功能标志，但用户在需要敏感数据追踪时被迫禁用诊断，失去关键可观测能力。count=1但影响为阻断性，P1。

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Circular Reference Error when running Process samples with SEMANTICKERNEL_EXPERIMENTAL_GENAI_ENABLE_OTEL_DIAGNOSTICS_SENSITIVE=true
source_issues.evidence: Setting SEMANTICKERNEL_EXPERIMENTAL_GENAI_ENABLE_OTEL_DIAGNOSTICS_SENSITIVE=true causes 'Circular reference detected' error on every function invocation in KernelProcessStep. KernelProcessStepContext object has reference loop preventing JSON serialization. Error occurs across all process execution variations (stateful steps, state loading).

signals.topic: Codex uses bwrap features incompatible with Ubuntu 22.04's bubblewrap version, blocking file editing on a common LTS distribution
signals.summary: Codex CLI (v0.116.0+) uses bwrap --argv0 and namespace features not supported in bubblewrap 0.6.1 (the version in Ubuntu 22.04 repositories). This makes the apply_patch tool non-functional and forces a degraded perl-based edit fallback. Users on a widely-deployed LTS Linux distribution cannot use the standard file editing workflow.
aliases: apply_patch bwrap namespace error on Ubuntu
signals.review_reason: Blocks standard file editing on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, one of the most widely deployed server Linux distributions. Two independent reporters confirm the issue — it is not an isolated case. The perl-based edit fallback represents a significantly degraded experience. Regression evidence in #15517 confirms this is a new breakage, not a pre-existing condition.

source_issues.title: Sandbox failure on Ubuntu 22.04: bwrap --argv0 not supported (bubblewrap 0.6.1)
source_issues.evidence: Issue #15551: Codex fails on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS with bwrap --argv0 not supported error. Standard file editing path is broken. Users forced to perl-based edit fallback. Two independent reporters (15551 and 15517) confirm this affects real users on Ubuntu 22.04.

source_issues.title: bwrap namespace error when using apply_patch
source_issues.evidence: Issue #15517: Regression after v0.116.0 update — bwrap namespace error on systems where user namespaces are restricted. apply_patch stops working, user forced to perl fallback. Confirmed regression from prior working state.

signals.topic: codex exec resume silently creates a new session instead of failing when given a nonexistent or ephemeral session ID
signals.summary: Passing a UUID that does not correspond to any existing session (or passing a thread_id from an ephemeral session) to codex exec resume does not return a 'not found' error. Instead, Codex silently creates a brand-new thread, runs the prompt, and exits 0. This makes automation unsafe because typos or stale IDs silently create fresh sessions with no error signal.
aliases: exec resume accepts invalid session IDs silently
signals.review_reason: Silent failure in automation is a dangerous pattern. A typo or stale ID in a resume command looks identical to a successful operation, creating a false sense that work was done in the intended session. In CI/automation contexts this can lead to data being written to the wrong session, audit trail corruption, and wasted API costs. The exit 0 makes this undetectable without manual transcript inspection.

source_issues.title: codex exec resume accepts nonexistent session ids and starts a new thread instead of failing
source_issues.evidence: Issue #15539: Passing a nonexistent UUID to codex exec resume silently creates a new session and exits 0. No error is returned. Automation scripts using resume cannot distinguish between a successful resume and a typo that created a fresh session.

source_issues.title: codex exec resume silently starts a new thread when given an ephemeral session id
source_issues.evidence: Issue #15538: Resuming an ephemeral session (codex exec --ephemeral) using its thread_id does not resume the ephemeral session. Instead a brand-new thread with a different thread_id is created. Users/automation believe they resumed a session when they started a fresh one with no prior context.

signals.topic: codex exec returns exit code 0 even when the executed command fails with a non-zero exit code
signals.summary: When codex exec runs a prompt that results in a shell command failing with a non-zero exit code, the failure is recorded in the JSON transcript (exit_code:1, status:"failed") but the outer codex exec process exits 0. This breaks CI/CD pipelines and scripting — callers cannot trust the process exit status to detect command failure.
aliases: codex exec ignores command exit status
signals.review_reason: Directly blocks CI/CD and automation pipelines. Exit code 0 on command failure is a fundamental contract violation — callers cannot programmatically detect that a command failed, making safe automation impossible. This is a primary workflow blocker for devops/CI use cases.

source_issues.title: codex exec exits 0 even when command_execution fails with nonzero exit code
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly documents that codex exec records exit_code:1 and status:failed in transcript but the process itself exits 0. Caller scripts/CI pipelines cannot detect failure.

signals.topic: codex cloud command fails with opaque 'Permission denied (os error 13)' when run in headless/non-TTY environments
signals.summary: When codex cloud is run without a TTY (e.g., in scripts, automation, CI runners, remote SSH), it exits with 'Error: Permission denied (os error 13)' instead of a helpful diagnostic. The same command works fine interactively. This makes the cloud command unusable in headless automation contexts where the CLI documentation explicitly directs users.
signals.review_reason: Blocks the primary automation path for cloud environment discovery. The error message is opaque and un-actionable (os error 13 gives no indication of the TTY requirement), making debugging in CI/automation impossible. This defeats the stated purpose of the cloud command in headless contexts.

source_issues.title: codex cloud fails with opaque 'Permission denied (os error 13)' when run headlessly
source_issues.evidence: Issue documents that the codex cloud command fails with os error 13 in non-TTY contexts, while working interactively. The CLI help explicitly directs users to 'codex cloud' for environment discovery, but that path is broken in automation.

signals.topic: codex exec -s read-only security boundary is bypassed for filesystem writes when run in a nested (parent) context
signals.summary: When codex exec -s read-only is launched from within an existing Codex session, the sandbox reports 'sandbox: read-only' and correctly blocks network access, but still allows filesystem writes. The read-only security policy is only partially enforced in nested contexts, creating an inconsistent and unsafe security boundary that undermines the read-only guarantee.
aliases: read-only policy bypass in nested exec
signals.review_reason: Security boundary violation: read-only mode provides a false sense of security when used in nested contexts. Filesystem writes that should be blocked are silently permitted. This fundamentally breaks the security guarantee that read-only mode is designed to provide. Any user relying on read-only mode to prevent accidental file modifications in nested workflows is exposed.

source_issues.title: codex exec -s read-only allows filesystem writes when nested under external sandbox
source_issues.evidence: Issue #15524: codex exec -s read-only blocks network access correctly but allows filesystem writes when nested. This is a security boundary violation — the read-only policy guarantee is broken in nested execution contexts, while it is correctly enforced in direct sandbox usage.

signals.topic: reasoning_content incompatibility causes 400 errors when passing model output across providers
signals.summary: Multi-turn tool-calling with non-DeepSeek reasoning models (Moonshot AI Kimi, Zhipu AI GLM) fails with 400 error. These models require reasoning_content in assistant messages on subsequent turns, but the SDK only handles this for DeepSeek. Affected users cannot use multi-turn tool-calling with these model providers.
aliases: reasoning model output to non-reasoning model 400
signals.review_reason: Two distinct failure modes share the same root cause: reasoning_content is mishandled when model output crosses provider or model-type boundaries. Both #2669 (Kimi multi-turn) and #569 (O4-mini to gpt-4.1 handoff) result in 400 API errors blocking core multi-turn/multi-agent workflows.

source_issues.title: `reasoning_content` support for models other than DeepSeek (GLM, Kimi, etc.)
source_issues.evidence: Moonshot AI Kimi models require reasoning_content in multi-turn tool calls; omitting it causes 400 error. Only DeepSeek is currently supported.

source_issues.title: Reasoning model items provide to General model
source_issues.evidence: When passing O4-mini agent output to gpt-4.1 agent, API returns 400 'Reasoning input items can only be provided to a reasoning or computer use model'. Multi-agent handoffs fail due to reasoning content incompatibility.

signals.topic: KeyError in _FunctionToolBatchExecutor under asyncio.eager_task_factory (Python 3.13 / Textual)
signals.summary: Parallel tool calls cause KeyError crash in Python 3.13+ when the event loop uses asyncio.eager_task_factory (e.g., Textual). The SDK registers task state after task creation, but eager tasks start synchronously, causing a race condition. Main workflow is blocked; workaround is downgrading to 0.9.3 or disabling parallel tool calls.
signals.review_reason: This is a regression in 0.12.5 that causes the main agent execution loop to crash (KeyError) when using parallel tool calls in Python 3.13+ with eager_task_factory. The issue blocks the core workflow, and the only workarounds (downgrade or disable parallel tools) represent significant functional degradation. Confirmed with detailed traceback and minimal repro.

source_issues.title: Regression in 0.12.5: KeyError in _FunctionToolBatchExecutor under asyncio.eager_task_factory (Textual / Python 3.13)
source_issues.evidence: SDK crashes with KeyError during parallel tool call execution. Workaround requires downgrading to 0.9.3 or disabling parallel tool calls — both are significant degradations for affected users. Reproduced on Python 3.13.2 with Textual TUI.

signals.topic: Traces silently dropped in long-running workers (Celery, FastAPI background tasks)
signals.summary: agents.trace() inside long-living processes (Celery, FastAPI background tasks, RQ, etc.) creates valid trace IDs but traces never appear on platform.openai.com/traces. The internal BatchTraceProcessor only flushes on process shutdown, which never happens in workers. No error is emitted, making the problem hard to discover.
aliases: tracing buffer never flushes in background workers
signals.review_reason: This causes a critical observability gap: traces are silently lost in any production deployment using background workers (Celery, FastAPI, RQ, Dramatiq). No error is raised, so users have no indication their traces are missing. This directly impacts production debugging and monitoring capability. Multiple production architectures are affected, and the problem is non-obvious to discover.

source_issues.title: Traces are silently dropped in long-running workers
source_issues.evidence: BatchTraceProcessor auto-flushes only on process shutdown. Long-running workers never shut down, so traces remain buffered forever. No error or warning is emitted. Identified by user who spent significant debugging effort; exact same code works as standalone script.

signals.topic: Guardrail response.cancel race condition: active response error in Realtime API
signals.summary: When guardrails trigger an interrupt with force_response_cancel=True, the SDK immediately sends the follow-up user input without waiting for response.done. On networks with latency, the server hasn't processed the cancel yet, causing 'Conversation already has an active response in progress' error. Reproduced with turn_detection.interrupt_response and after upgrading to 0.4.1.
aliases: active response in progress error after guardrail
signals.review_reason: This causes guardrail-protected Realtime API conversations to fail intermittently based on network latency. The failure is reproducible and blocks the guardrail interrupt + follow-up flow. References prior duplicate reports (#1907, #1912), indicating this is a recurring real-world problem.

source_issues.title: Guardrail follow-up can race with response.cancel completion
source_issues.evidence: User hit 'Conversation already has an active response in progress' error when using turn_detection.interrupt_response. Same error reported by another commenter on related PR. References #1907 and #1912 as prior instances.

signals.topic: SQLAlchemySession race conditions drop writes under concurrent access
signals.summary: SQLAlchemySession has two race conditions: (1) _ensure_tables() can fail with 'table already exists' when multiple tasks concurrently initialize the same fresh session, and (2) add_items() can fail with UNIQUE constraint violation, losing writes. A minimal repro with 25 concurrent workers shows both failures and dropped items.
signals.review_reason: This causes data loss in concurrent session access scenarios — a common production pattern. The repro confirms both failure modes and that some writes are silently dropped. This directly impacts session persistence reliability.

source_issues.title: SQLAlchemySession can fail and drop writes on concurrent first access
source_issues.evidence: Minimal repro with 25 concurrent workers shows OperationalError 'table already exists' and IntegrityError 'UNIQUE constraint failed: agent_sessions.session_id'. Stored item count is well below submitted writes — data loss confirmed.

signals.topic: Batch API large result file download fails with ConnectionResetError (>200MB)
signals.summary: 用户在下载 Batch API 的大型结果文件（>200MB）时，连接被对端重置（ConnectionResetError / RemoteProtocolError），导致无法获取批量处理结果。主流程阻断，用户被迫手动实现分片下载 workaround。
aliases: Batch API large file download fails
Batch result file streaming broken for large outputs
signals.review_reason: 这是明确的主流程阻断问题。用户提交批量任务后无法下载结果文件（>200MB 时连接被重置），被迫手动拆分 batch 规避，这是关键功能不可用的直接证据。count=1 因该文件仅含 1 条，但高影响力（主流程阻断、500-1000MB 处丢包、无 SDK 内置修复）足以支撑 P0。

source_issues.title: bug: Batch API result file download fails for large outputs (>200MB) with ConnectionResetError
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告 50k embedding 请求批量完成后，下载结果文件时连接在 ~500-1000MB 处被重置，抛出 httpcore.RemoteProtocolError: peer closed connection without sending complete message body。Workaround: 需将请求拆分为 10k 一批以避免超过 200MB 文件大小限制。明确的主流程阻断。

signals.topic: Web fetch tool silently drops content inside custom HTML elements (web components)
signals.summary: 使用 Web Components/Angular/Lit 等自定义 HTML 元素构建的网页，其内容在 web fetch 工具中被完全丢弃（仅返回 <title>），用户无法获取有意义内容。
aliases: Web fetch skips custom HTML element subtrees
AI fetch tool loses content from web components pages
signals.review_reason: 虽然issue在openai-python仓库但web fetch功能属于上层应用（claude.ai/ChatGPT），Python SDK不一定是根因。然而issue被标记为bug且用户明确选'Python library issue'，有明确用户影响（现代网站内容完全不可读、静默丢数据无错误提示），属于关键功能不可用。保留为P1，置信度0.7（因根因归属有歧义）。

source_issues.title: AI Web Fetch Tools Silently Drop Content Inside Custom HTML Elements
source_issues.evidence: 用户验证：curl/Grok/Claude Code WebFetch/Google crawler 均正常返回页面内容，唯独 claude.ai 和 ChatGPT web fetch 仅返回 <title> 标签，完全丢弃自定义元素内的所有文本内容（静默数据丢失，无错误提示）。影响所有使用 Web Components/Angular/Lit 框架构建的现代网站。

signals.topic: Control UI assets missing from npm package, making web dashboard inaccessible after upgrading to v2026.3.22
signals.summary: The dist/control-ui/ directory is not included in the published v2026.3.22 npm tarball, causing all npm-installed users to see 'Control UI assets not found' error. Both fresh installs and upgrades are affected.
signals.review_reason: This is a packaging regression that blocks the primary web dashboard for every npm-installed user upgrading to v2026.3.22. Two independent users reported this, both rolled back to v2026.3.13. Root cause is confirmed: dist/control-ui/ was excluded from the npm tarball due to a build/files configuration issue in the dashboard v2 rewrite.

source_issues.title: v2026.3.22: Control UI assets missing from npm package (dashboard v2 regression)
source_issues.evidence: The dist/control-ui/ directory (index.html, CSS, JS assets) is not included in the published v2026.3.22 npm tarball. Verified by comparing tarballs: v2026.3.13 includes the directory, v2026.3.22 does not. Root cause identified as a files/.npmignore misconfiguration in the dashboard v2 rewrite. User rolled back to v2026.3.13 as workaround.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: v2026.3.13 upgrade to 2026.3.22 error: Control UI assets not found
source_issues.evidence: Separate user report of the same regression: upgrading from v2026.3.13 to v2026.3.22 results in Control UI assets not found error, making the web dashboard inaccessible.

signals.topic: Session lane lock not released after API error (529 overload), making session permanently unresponsive
signals.summary: When an Anthropic API call returns a 529 (service overloaded) error, the session lane lock is never released. Sessions become permanently unresponsive to new messages until manually reset via /reset, losing all conversation history.
aliases: lane lock not released on 529 error
session permanently stuck after API error
signals.review_reason: High-severity session state bug causing complete session deadlock. Observed 3 times in one day across different channel sessions. Root cause clearly identified: lane lock not in a finally block. No workaround that preserves conversation history — only /reset works, which destroys all history. Not P0 only because count=1 and single repo, but user impact is severe (permanent unresponsiveness with data loss on reset).

source_issues.title: Session lane lock not released after API error (529 overload)
source_issues.evidence: Observed 3 times in one day. When API returns 529, run ends with isError=true but lane lock stays held. New messages trigger 'lane wait exceeded' with queueAhead=0 indefinitely. Only /reset works, which loses all conversation history. Log evidence: 'lane wait exceeded: lane=session:agent:main:discord:channel:1481740414921867345 waitedMs=81485 queueAhead=0' followed by 'embedded run agent end: isError=true error=The AI service is temporarily overloaded'.

signals.topic: Gateway OAuth re-authorization on every startup burns refresh tokens, making openai-codex provider permanently unavailable
signals.summary: Gateway initiates a full browser OAuth re-authorization flow on every startup, invalidating the existing refresh token before any user request. This creates an unbreakable failure loop with no reliable workaround for systemd service users.
signals.review_reason: Provider-level failure making a specific model (openai-codex/gpt-5.4) completely non-functional when running the gateway as a persistent service. The token is burned on every startup, creating an unbreakable failure loop. This is the recommended production setup (systemd service), leaving affected users with no reliable path forward.

source_issues.title: Gateway initiates full OAuth re-authorization on every startup, invalidating existing refresh token before first request
source_issues.evidence: On every gateway startup, auth.openai.com/oauth/authorize URL opens in browser before any user request. This invalidates the refresh token. On first request, 401 refresh_token_reused error appears. The same error hash appears on every failure across multiple restarts. The issue affects openai-codex provider running as a systemd service, which is the recommended production setup. No reliable workaround exists.

signals.topic: CLI commands crash gateway via WebSocket handshake timeout when Telegram polling is active
signals.summary: Running any openclaw CLI command (cron list, gateway status, etc.) while the gateway is serving Telegram long-polling causes a WebSocket handshake timeout that crashes the entire gateway process with close code 1000.
signals.review_reason: Process-level crash triggered by routine CLI operations. Any CLI command (cron list, gateway status, etc.) crashes the entire gateway when Telegram polling is active. This blocks routine operational workflows and requires users to work around the gateway's own CLI. The gateway should handle CLI connections gracefully without crashing.

source_issues.title: CLI commands crash gateway via WebSocket handshake timeout
source_issues.evidence: Running 'openclaw cron list' while gateway is serving Telegram polling: handshake timeout (3001ms) followed by 'gateway closed (1000)' — full gateway process terminates. Workaround: avoid all CLI commands while gateway is running, or read cron config directly from ~/.openclaw/cron/jobs.json. Also observed polling stall (106.72s without getUpdates) as a precursor pattern.

signals.topic: File attachments silently dropped on Discord after v2026.3.22 upgrade — tool reports success but no file uploaded
signals.summary: The message tool's filePath, media, and filename parameters silently drop file attachments on Discord. The tool returns {ok: true} with a valid messageId, but the message arrives with empty attachments array. This is a regression from v2026.3.13.
aliases: filePath media filename not working on Discord
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss regression: the message tool reports success but files are never delivered to Discord. Users have no indication of failure since the tool returns {ok: true}. No workaround exists — file attachments via the message tool simply do not work on Discord in v2026.3.22.

source_issues.title: [Bug] message tool file attachments silently dropped on Discord after v2026.3.22
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression from v2026.3.13 where file sending worked. Tool returns {ok: true} with messageId but message has 'attachments: []'. Direct Discord REST API upload via curl works fine, confirming the issue is in the message tool layer. filePath schema description says 'Telegram only' — suspected root cause. .docx file (19KB) consistently fails.

signals.topic: Windows: Uncaught NotImplementedError when using absolute/absolute-like patterns with /add or /read-only commands
signals.summary: On Windows, using /add or /read-only with absolute or non-relative glob patterns raises an uncaught NotImplementedError from Python's pathlib.py, crashing the main workflow.
signals.review_reason: P0: Two confirmed crash reports from Windows users on /add and /read-only commands — both raise uncaught NotImplementedError from pathlib.py line 1090. Both are main workflow blockers (file operations). Count=2, Windows-only, confirmed in separate issues with full stack traces.

source_issues.title: Uncaught NotImplementedError in pathlib.py line 1090
source_issues.evidence: NotImplementedError: Non-relative patterns are unsupported — crashes on /add command on Windows 11, blocking file addition workflow

source_issues.title: Uncaught NotImplementedError in pathlib.py line 1090
source_issues.evidence: Same NotImplementedError on /read-only command on Windows 10, crashes main loop

signals.topic: Git config lock permission errors block aider startup on Windows and Linux
signals.summary: Aider fails to start with OSError: Permission denied on git config.lock files, preventing the tool from initializing in environments where .git/config is not writable or lock files are held.
aliases: Permission denied git config.lock startup crash
signals.review_reason: P0: Two confirmed startup crashes across Linux and Windows where aider cannot even initialize because git config lock file is inaccessible. Blocks the entire application from running. Issues #4947 and #4944 are the same root cause (util.py line 1054). Note: #4943 appears to be a duplicate of #4944 (same author, same trace, same day).

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in util.py line 1054
source_issues.evidence: PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/home/rodolfo/.git/config.lock' — aider cannot start, fails at setup_git()

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in util.py line 1054
source_issues.evidence: Same OSError on Windows at 'C:\WINDOWS\system32\.git\config.lock' — aider cannot start, blocks all usage

signals.topic: Windows: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError when rendering special Unicode characters (e.g. \u2588 block character) to Windows console
signals.summary: On Windows, special Unicode characters in tool output (e.g. block characters) cause an uncaught UnicodeEncodeError from cp1252 codec, crashing the entire application.
signals.review_reason: P1: Confirmed crash on Windows when tool output contains special Unicode characters (e.g. block chars). Full application terminates — not just the lint step. Clear user impact and reproducibility on Windows cp1252 console. Count=1 but crash severity is high.

source_issues.title: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in cp1252.py line 19
source_issues.evidence: UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '\u2588' in position 39 — crashes during lint warning output on Windows 11 with cp1252 console encoding, full application terminates

signals.topic: Uncaught TypeError in analytics.py — app crashes on launch due to duplicate 'distinct_id' argument
signals.summary: Aider crashes immediately on launch with TypeError: Client.capture() got multiple values for argument 'distinct_id', preventing any use of the tool.
signals.review_reason: P1: App crashes on launch — the analytics.event('launched') call at startup is broken, causing immediate termination. High severity as it blocks any usage. Count=1 but complete startup failure.

source_issues.title: Uncaught TypeError in analytics.py line 240
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: Client.capture() got multiple values for argument 'distinct_id' — occurs at launch (main.py line 664, analytics.event('launched')), app terminates immediately

signals.topic: Custom OpenAI provider via litellm fails with authentication error — API KEY is forced regardless of provider configuration
signals.summary: When using a custom_openai/<model> with litellm as the provider backend, aider incorrectly forces an API KEY check and ignores litellm's own authentication, preventing users from using their configured litellm endpoint.
aliases: API KEY forced for custom provider litellm
signals.review_reason: P1: Blocks usage of litellm custom_openai provider — a legitimate integration path for users who want to use aider with their own LLM backends via litellm. Authentication failure is a clear user-impact issue preventing the main workflow (LLM interaction).

source_issues.title: Aider does not ignore API KEY when using custom_openai provider from litellm

signals.topic: Redteam scan fails when using self-hosted OpenAI-compatible API key — remote generation mandate blocks local execution

High frequency (recurring across two distinct users) + main flow blocking + sample links present = P0.

signals.topic: SimplePropertyGraphStore crashes on Windows with UnicodeEncodeError when persisting UTF-8 content

signals.topic: Swarm/hive-mind multi-agent orchestration system fundamentally non-functional
signals.summary: v3 rewrite replaced the v2 execution engine (SwarmOrchestrator + subprocess management) with flat JSON CRUD. Agents spawn and tasks are created/assigned, but no subprocess is ever spawned to execute work. Workers stay permanently idle (0 tasks, 0 tokens), queen load reports Math.random(), and agent stores are disconnected from task stores.
aliases: Swarm agents do not execute work
MCP tool prefix mismatch in spawn prompt
signals.review_reason: 4 related issues all describing the swarm orchestration core loop as broken. The v3 rewrite replaced a working execution engine with metadata-only CRUD. Agents spawn, tasks are assigned, but nothing executes. Queen load is Math.random(), worker status is hardcoded, tool prefixes are wrong, agent stores are disconnected. The entire observability and execution pipeline for the multi-agent swarm system is non-functional.

source_issues.title: Swarm agents still do not execute work — v3.5.42
source_issues.evidence: Multiple test cases (MCP tools, CLI swarm start, fresh session POC) all produce identical result: agents 'spawned' with status idle, 0 active, 0 tasks, 0 tokens. No files created. v3 rewrite replaced the v2 execution engine (SwarmOrchestrator + EventEmitter + subprocess management) with flat JSON CRUD — nothing dispatches work to a Claude subprocess.

source_issues.title: Hive-mind worker tracking is non-functional: task lifecycle never syncs agent state
source_issues.evidence: task_assign writes to tasks/store.json but never updates agents.json → workers permanently idle, currentTask stays null. task_complete never increments taskCount. hive-mind_status returns Math.random() for queen load. task-tools.ts and hive-mind-tools.ts operate on separate JSON files with zero cross-references.

source_issues.title: v3 regression: hive-mind_status hardcodes all workers as idle
source_issues.evidence: Status handler hardcodes status:'idle', tasksCompleted:0 for every worker regardless of actual state. Never reads from agent store. Referenced as blocking issue across multiple duplicate reports (#762, #758, #655, #588, #330). Dual store problem: hive-mind_spawn writes to agents.json while agent_spawn writes to agents/store.json — disconnected.

source_issues.title: hive-mind spawn --claude prompt hardcodes wrong MCP tool prefix

Additionally 2 phantom tools referenced that don't exist under any prefix. MCP serverInfo.name still reports 'claude-flow' instead of 'ruflo' during handshake.

signals.topic: Headless workers 100% failure rate + daemon accumulation causing kernel panic
signals.summary: stdin pipe never closed (stdio:['pipe','pipe','pipe']) → all headless worker invocations hang until SIGTERM (exit 143). No PID singleton enforcement for daemons → they accumulate across sessions/projects. Combined with worker failures: 9 hung processes at ~3GB each + 8 daemon processes = 71GB RSS on a 36GB machine → kernel panic (watchdog timeout: no checkins from watchdogd in 91 seconds).
signals.review_reason: Explicit, quantified user impact: 100% worker failure rate across 68 executions, 71GB RSS on a 36GB machine (193% RAM oversubscription), kernel panic with watchdog timeout. Documented system crash at scale. Multiple interacting bugs compound into unrecoverable resource exhaustion. P0 despite count=1 because review_reason provides strong user impact evidence (kernel panic, production system crash).

source_issues.title: [Bug] Workers always fail (stdin never closed) + daemons never terminate = kernel panic at scale
source_issues.evidence: 68 worker executions: audit 100% failure rate (exit 143 SIGTERM), optimize 95% failure rate. On a 36GB Mac with 8 projects: 9 hung processes at ~3GB each + 8 daemon processes = 71GB RSS (193% of physical RAM) → kernel panic (watchdog timeout: no checkins from watchdogd in 91 seconds). Root causes: stdin pipe never closed, no PID singleton for daemons, config.yaml silently ignored.

signals.topic: MCP server crashes on startup (self-SIGKILL) — all MCP tool usage blocked
signals.summary: getStatus() returns {running:true, pid:process.pid} for stdio transport. Start command then does process.kill(existingStatus.pid, 'SIGKILL') — killing its own PID. Every npx ruflo@latest mcp start invocation crashes immediately. All MCP integrations (Claude Code, VSCode Copilot, programmatic clients) are blocked.
signals.review_reason: Complete startup crash preventing any MCP tool usage. All MCP integrations (Claude Code, VSCode Copilot, programmatic clients) are blocked. Deterministic crash on every startup — a hard blocker for any MCP use case. While fixed in v3.5.39, users on v3.5.37/38 are affected.

source_issues.title: MCP server self-kills on startup (SIGKILL to own PID)
source_issues.evidence: npx ruflo@latest mcp start crashes immediately: '[INFO] Starting MCP Server... [WARN] MCP Server (PID: 91320) - restarting... Killed'. Root cause: getStatus() returns {running:true, pid:process.pid} for stdio transport. Start command then does process.kill(existingStatus.pid, 'SIGKILL') — killing its own PID. Verified in Docker (node:20-slim). Affects v3.5.37 and v3.5.38.

signals.topic: AgentDB bridge unavailable — entire AgentDB feature inaccessible to users

signals.review_reason: Full feature (all agentdb_* tools) is inaccessible to users. Root cause clearly identified. Doctor command misleadingly passes. Not P0 because count=1 and it's a secondary feature, but clearly significant with no user-visible error pointing to the real cause.

aliases: LLM structured output schema missing required fields
zod4Schema required array empty causing incomplete JSON from LLMs
structured output missing fields due to io input mode
