source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows delta.content as array with thinking parts from Mistral Small 4 via Ollama, causing TypeValidationError 'expected string, received array' in both doGenerate and doStream flows.

signals.topic: Race condition in attemptClose causes stream enqueue error and crashes
signals.summary: In runToolsTransformation, attemptClose() can be called multiple times when multiple tool executions complete concurrently, causing TypeError 'stream is not in a state that permits enqueue'. Fire-and-forget .then()/.catch() callbacks also race against stream closing. Reproducible in Convex V8 isolates and when aborting and restarting streams.
aliases: tool execution stream controller closed error
signals.review_reason: This is a runtime crash (TypeError) that causes streamText to fail non-deterministically when multiple tools execute concurrently. The race condition is well-documented with a root cause analysis, and the crash is explicitly shown in the error. This blocks tool-use workflows in concurrent environments.

source_issues.title: Race condition in attemptClose causes 'stream is not in a state that permits enqueue'
source_issues.evidence: TypeError explicitly shown with stack trace pointing to attemptClose in run-tools-transformation.ts. Root cause analysis describes interleaving of flush() and .finally() callbacks on concurrent tool executions. Reproducible in Convex V8 isolate environment.

signals.topic: sendAutomaticallyWhen permanently stalls when tool approval is denied (approved:false missing from state check)
signals.summary: When using sendAutomaticallyWhen:lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithApprovalResponses, denying a tool call via addToolApprovalResponse({approved:false}) causes the predicate to permanently return false. The output-denied state is missing from the .every() check, so denied tools are treated as still pending.
aliases: tool denial causes conversation to hang
signals.review_reason: This causes a complete UX blockage: once a user denies a tool approval, the entire chat interface permanently freezes and no further messages can be sent. The predicate failure is unambiguous and the fix is clearly identified. This is a critical flow blocker for approval-based tool workflows.

source_issues.title: Bug: `sendAutomaticallyWhen` never fires when any tool approval is denied
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: output-denied state is missing from the .every() check in lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithApprovalResponses.ts. The predicate never returns true after denial, permanently stalling the conversation.

signals.topic: Standalone mode: NextResponse.rewrite() in middleware returns 307 redirect instead of transparently serving rewritten content, causing infinite redirect loop
signals.summary: Standalone server does not process x-middleware-rewrite internally — rewrites are exposed as 307 redirects to the client. Works in dev, fails in standalone production.
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure: middleware rewrites are a core routing feature that works in dev but breaks in standalone production mode. This is a deployment-blocking regression affecting any standalone deployment using NextResponse.rewrite(), including internationalization middleware (next-intl). Count=2 valid issues with reproducible evidence.

source_issues.title: Standalone mode: NextResponse.rewrite() in middleware returns 307 instead of serving rewritten content
source_issues.evidence: Standalone server returns HTTP 307 with location: / and x-middleware-rewrite header. Client receives redirect instead of rewritten content. Infinite loop in browser. Dev server (next dev) handles correctly. Confirmed reproducible via curl commands.

source_issues.title: Standalone mode: NextResponse.rewrite() in middleware returns 307 instead of transparently serving rewritten content
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction with next-intl middleware shows 307 Temporary Redirect with location: / to client. Causes infinite redirect loop. Same code works in next dev. Affects standalone production deployments behind nginx.

signals.topic: app/favicon.ico scaffold conflicts with unstable_instant validation; build error message does not name the conflicting file
signals.summary: create-next-app scaffolds app/favicon.ico by default. When cacheComponents: true and unstable_instant is used, the build fails with a generic error that does not identify the problematic file (app/favicon.ico). Users must guess and manually remove the file.
signals.review_reason: Poor error message quality causing significant debugging friction. The error is caused by a create-next-app scaffold file that users don't know to look for. Two valid issues confirm the problem. While there's a workaround, the generic error with no filename is a clear developer experience failure that should be fixed.

source_issues.title: app/favicon.ico scaffold conflicts with unstable_instant validation; build error doesn't name the file
source_issues.evidence: Build fails with generic 'Runtime data such as cookies(), headers(), params... accessed inside generateMetadata' error. No filename, no suggested fix. Cause is app/favicon.ico created by create-next-app. Workaround exists (move to metadata.icons) but error message gives no direction.

source_issues.title: app/favicon.ico scaffold conflicts with unstable_instant validation; error message doesn't name the file
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate report confirming the same issue. Error message does not identify app/favicon.ico as the source of the conflict.

signals.topic: Turbopack HMR stops working after first edit for dynamically imported JSON files (16.2 regression)
signals.summary: Dynamic import() with template literals for JSON files only triggers HMR once. Subsequent edits are silently ignored until dev server restart. Common pattern with next-intl i18n files.
aliases: turbopack HMR JSON hot reload regression
signals.review_reason: Core development workflow blocked: HMR is essential for dev productivity. This is a confirmed regression from 16.1 to 16.2 where dynamic import() for JSON files (common in i18n patterns like next-intl) only hot-reloads once. Users must restart the dev server after every file change, severely degrading DX. Despite count=1, the regression evidence and widespread pattern justify P0.

source_issues.title: Turbopack HMR stops working after first edit for dynamically imported JSON files (16.2 regression)
source_issues.evidence: First JSON file edit triggers HMR update correctly. Second edit silently ignored. Requires dev server restart to restore HMR. Root cause: Server Fast Refresh uses Turbopack's fine-grained module graph which cannot statically analyze template literal dynamic imports. Regression from 16.1 to 16.2.

signals.topic: turbopackInferModuleSideEffects causes all serverless functions to fall back from Bun to Node.js, resulting in 500 errors in production
signals.summary: PR #87216 enabled turbopackInferModuleSideEffects in stable builds (16.2.0). Turbopack's AST analyzer detects top-level Bun globals as side effects, forcing Node.js runtime in all Lambda bundles where Bun.redis is referenced, causing ReferenceError at runtime.
signals.review_reason: Production deployment failure: ALL serverless functions return 500 errors after upgrading to 16.2.0. Root cause is a single PR changing a Turbopack inference flag from canary-only to stable. This is a main flow failure (every route broken) with no indication of the root cause from error messages. Despite count=1, the severity (all functions, 500 errors, production-blocking) justifies P0.

source_issues.title: 16.2.0 regression: turbopackInferModuleSideEffects causes all Bun functions to fall back to Node.js
source_issues.evidence: Every serverless function returns 500 Internal Server Error at runtime after upgrading from 16.1.6 to 16.2.0. Vercel deploys switch from Bun 1.x to Node.js 24.x at runtime. Bun.redis is undefined in Node context, causing ReferenceError. All functions affected (Page, API, _error, data). Detailed comparison table shows clear regression.

signals.topic: Dev server silently exits (exit code 0) with cacheComponents + Turbopack on Node 24, leaving no error trace
signals.summary: Combination of Turbopack and cacheComponents: true on Node 24 causes the dev server to start, print 'Ready', then immediately exit cleanly with code 0. No error message, no stack trace.
aliases: next dev exit code 0 turbopack node 24
signals.review_reason: Main flow failure: dev server immediately exits with no error message when using Turbopack + cacheComponents on Node 24. This completely blocks development. The clean exit code (0) makes it especially hard to detect as a bug — users may assume the server started and is listening. NODE_DEBUG evidence confirms connections torn down, ruling out startup delay.

source_issues.title: Dev server silently exits (code 0) with cacheComponents + Turbopack on Node 24
source_issues.evidence: Server prints 'Ready in ~200ms' then exits cleanly (exit code 0). No crash message. NODE_DEBUG=net shows connections torn down immediately. Workaround: use --webpack. cacheComponents works fine with webpack alone; Turbopack works fine without cacheComponents. Only the combination on Node 24 fails.

signals.topic: turbo ls --affected reports all packages as changed due to false positives on root config files
signals.summary: `turbo ls --affected` incorrectly marks ALL packages as affected when only workspace dependencies (e.g., sass version bump) are updated, because it falsely detects the root package.json as changed even when git confirms it was not modified. Breaks CI/CD affected-package detection.
aliases: affected command accuracy bug root config changes
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow CI/CD blocking bug. `turbo ls --affected` is specifically designed for CI to determine which packages need rebuilding — when it reports all packages as affected for trivial changes, it defeats the entire purpose of incremental builds and wastes massive CI compute time. Both reported cases show git-confirmed evidence that root package.json was NOT changed, yet turbo incorrectly marks it as changed. With count=2 and a real production CI run cited as evidence, this is P0.

source_issues.title: turbo ls --affected reports all packages changed due to false positive on root package.json when only workspace dependencies changed
source_issues.evidence: In a real CI run, Renovate bot updated sass in apps/web/package.json. Git diff confirmed only 2 files changed (apps/web/package.json, yarn.lock). But `turbo ls --affected` reported ALL 11 packages as affected. DEBUG output showed 'DefaultGlobalFileChanged { file: AnchoredSystemPathBuf(package.json) }' even though git confirmed root package.json was not modified.

source_issues.title: ls --affected accuracy issue when root package.json or turbo.json changes
source_issues.evidence: After adding a space to root package.json, `turbo ls --affected` shows ALL packages as affected. Meanwhile `turbo build --dry-run=json` correctly shows all packages as cache HIT. The bug causes entire monorepo to be rebuilt in CI when only one package's dependency changed.

signals.topic: turbo watch causes cascading task restarts in deep dependency graphs, garbling TUI
signals.summary: When running `turbo watch dev`, tasks restart exponentially in deep dependency graphs because watch detects dist/ output changes as source file changes, triggering dependent task restarts that cascade through every layer. On Windows this renders the TUI completely unreadable with garbled output.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking bug that makes `turbo watch` unusable in monorepos with deep dependency chains. It causes exponential redundant task restarts that waste build time AND renders the TUI completely unreadable on Windows (ConPTY can't handle rapid redraws). The issue is reproducible, has a minimal repro repo, and explicitly contrasts with `turbo run dev` which works correctly — confirming this is a watch-specific regression.

source_issues.title: turbo watch triggers cascading task restarts in deep dependency graphs, garbling TUI
source_issues.evidence: Tasks restart multiple times in rapid succession, producing garbled TUI with merged task names and exit codes. Affects both initial watch run and edits to low-level dependencies. `turbo run dev` does NOT have this problem.

signals.topic: Turborepo installation fails on Windows due to missing Windows binaries
signals.summary: On native Windows (non-WSL), `npm install turbo` installs successfully but the turbo binary cannot be found at runtime. Turbo looks for turbo-windows-64 but only finds Linux binaries, preventing any use of the tool on Windows.
aliases: Windows binary not found on install
signals.review_reason: This is a startup crash that completely prevents Turbo from running on native Windows. The tool cannot be used at all — it fails immediately at binary resolution. This is a fundamental platform compatibility issue, not an edge case. Despite being count=1, the severity is extreme (complete tool breakage on a major OS), and the issue has 12 comments confirming broad Windows user impact.

source_issues.title: Turborepo Installation Fails on Windows - Missing Binaries
source_issues.evidence: npm install completes but turbo build fails with 'Turborepo did not find the correct binary for your platform (windows 64). We were not able to find the binary at: turbo-windows-64/bin/turbo.exe. Found unnecessary binaries for other platforms: turbo-linux-64/bin/turbo.' Same setup works in WSL 2.0, proving it's Windows-specific. 12 comments confirming the issue affects multiple Windows 11 users.

signals.topic: Persistent tasks (dev servers) terminate prematurely after upgrade, breaking local development
signals.summary: After upgrading from 2.8.17 to 2.8.18, `persistent: true` tasks (e.g., Vite dev server) stop immediately after starting instead of running continuously. Regressed in 2.8.18 and affects multiple development workflows.
aliases: dev server exits immediately persistent task stops
vite dev stops after starting turbo 2.8.18
signals.review_reason: This is a clear regression in 2.8.18 that breaks the core local development workflow — persistent dev servers must stay running, but they terminate immediately. The version pinning evidence (2.8.17 works, 2.8.18+ broken) confirms this is a regression. Combined with the historically related #7279 (23 comments, same issue pattern with Vite), this represents a recurring reliability problem for the most fundamental local development use case. While count=1, the regression evidence and developer workflow impact justify P1.

source_issues.title: Persistent config no longer works
source_issues.evidence: Last working version: 2.8.17. `npx turbo@2.8.17 renderer-dev` works, `npx turbo@2.8.18 renderer-dev` and `2.8.19` do not. Vite dev server (with `persistent: true`) stops soon after running. 14 comments discussing the regression. A historically related issue #7279 had 23 comments showing this is a recurring regression pattern for persistent tasks.

signals.topic: Remote cache is not used when entry task has cache disabled, preventing cache uploads of downstream tasks
signals.summary: When the root/entry task has `cache: false`, the remote cache is not used at all — downstream subtasks with cache enabled also fail to upload/download from remote cache. This breaks the remote caching workflow in monorepos where not all tasks should be cached.
aliases: remote cache bypass when root task cache off
subtask remote cache not uploaded entry task no cache
signals.review_reason: Remote caching is a core Turborepo feature. When a root-level task disables cache, downstream tasks that DO have cache enabled fail to upload to remote cache — this breaks the entire remote caching workflow for affected teams and causes unnecessary rebuilds. The bug is clearly reproducible with a dedicated repo. P1 (not P0) because it's not a full tool breakage, but the cache-miss cost in CI environments is significant.

source_issues.title: remote cache isn't used when the entry task has cache off
source_issues.evidence: User has a root task 'main' with cache:false, and a subtask 'sub-task-1' with cache enabled. Expected: sub-task-1's cache should be uploaded to remote. Actual: sub-task-1 is not cached remotely. Repro repo provided with company remote cache service.

signals.topic: Next.js Turbopack prebuilt deployments fail at runtime due to missing vendored context files
signals.summary: When using `vercel build` + `vercel deploy --prebuilt` with Turbopack and Pages Router, vendored context files (e.g. head-manager-context.js) are missing from serverless function bundles, causing MODULE_NOT_FOUND runtime errors on any page using next/head or next/error. The root cause is that @vercel/next's fallback to @vercel/nft static analysis does not trace require-hook.js path rewrites, while next-minimal-server.js.nft.json (which correctly includes all vendored files) is only consumed when the undocumented VERCEL_NEXT_BUNDLED_SERVER=1 env var is set — which never happens during prebuilt builds.
aliases: Pages Router vendored context files missing in prebuilt deployments
signals.review_reason: 用户 prebuilt 部署 + Turbopack 时 Pages Router 核心功能运行时崩溃，阻断页面渲染。错误路径清晰（require-hook.js 路径重写被 nft fallback 遗漏 + 未记录 env var 门控）。影响所有使用 prebuilt 部署 + Turbopack + Pages Router 的 Next.js 用户，无开箱即用解决方案。

source_issues.title: Prebuilt deployments with Turbopack miss vendored Pages Router context files at runtime
source_issues.evidence: Runtime MODULE_NOT_FOUND for vendored context files. Breaks next/head and next/error in Pages Router production deployments. Workaround requires manual outputFileTracingIncludes configuration.

signals.topic: vercel domains add 拒绝认领已删除项目的 .vercel.app 子域名，导致域名管理流程阻断
signals.summary: 删除项目并重建同名项目后，vercel domains add 拒绝将 .vercel.app 子域名分配给新项目，报错 'already assigned to another project'，但 vercel alias set 能在同一团队下成功认领同一子域名。--force 标志也无效。子域名陷入 alias set 可路由但 domains add 不可分配的矛盾状态，用户无法完成域名绑定主流程。
aliases: domains add fails for orphaned .vercel.app subdomains
子域名在删除项目后无法重新绑定
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：用户在删除并重建同名项目后无法将 .vercel.app 子域名绑定到新项目。vercel alias set 能成功证明子域名在团队范围内，但 domains add 仍拒绝，暗示后端存在孤立记录未正确清理。--force 标志无效，用户无任何自助解决方案。

source_issues.title: vercel domains add fails for .vercel.app subdomain that vercel alias set can claim
source_issues.evidence: vercel domains add 在项目重建场景下阻断，alias set 可工作但 domains add 不可用，用户无法完成域名绑定主流程。--force 标志也无法绕过。

signals.topic: Vercel Serverless 函数无法连接 MongoDB Atlas（即便 IP 白名单设为 0.0.0.0/0）
signals.summary: 从 Vercel Serverless 函数连接 MongoDB Atlas 时，即使 Atlas IP 白名单已设为 0.0.0.0/0（允许所有 IP），Mongoose 仍报 MongooseServerSelectionError: ReplicaSetNoPrimary，无法建立数据库连接。本地环境连接正常，仅 Vercel 部署环境失败。根本原因疑似 Vercel Serverless 环境的动态 IP 或 DNS 解析问题。
aliases: MongoDB Atlas connection fails from Vercel serverless
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：所有依赖 MongoDB 的 Serverless 函数在生产环境完全失败，应用无法运行。用户已排除 IP 白名单配置问题（设为 0.0.0.0/0），本地环境正常，指向 Vercel Serverless 环境的动态 IP/DNS 问题。此类问题反复出现在 Vercel + MongoDB 组合中。

source_issues.title: MongoDB/Mongoose Connection Fails on Vercel Despite IP Whitelist Set to 0.0.0.0/0
source_issues.evidence: 生产环境所有依赖 MongoDB 的 Serverless 函数全部失败，应用完全不可用。本地正常，Vercel 环境失败，排除了配置错误可能性。

signals.topic: Go to Definition opens new buffer instead of navigating within same file
signals.summary: Core navigation shortcut 'Go to Definition' opens a new buffer instead of scrolling to the definition within the same file, breaking fundamental IDE navigation workflow.
aliases: Go to Definition new tab instead of jump
signals.review_reason: Breaks a fundamental code navigation flow that is central to daily IDE usage. Users cannot navigate within a file using Go to Definition — a core productivity feature. Count is 1 but user impact is high as it affects every occurrence of this common workflow.

source_issues.title: Go to definitions opens new buffer every time (within same file)
source_issues.evidence: Core navigation shortcut 'Go to Definition' opens a new buffer instead of scrolling to the definition within the same file. User reports it worked differently a few weeks ago. Affects TypeScript files. Breaks fundamental IDE navigation workflow.

signals.topic: Remote ACP agent cannot access MCP tools configured in settings
signals.summary: When connected to a remote project over SSH, Zed launches MCP stdio instances locally instead of passing MCP configuration to the remote ACP agent, making the combined remote ACP + remote MCP workflow completely non-functional.
aliases: MCP not passed to remote ACP agent
zed launches local MCP instead of passing to remote agent
signals.review_reason: Complete breakage of a documented remote development workflow combining ACP agents with MCP tools. Users relying on remote SSH development with AI agent capabilities cannot use MCP tools at all through the ACP agent. Blocks the primary use case of Zed as a remote AI coding assistant.

source_issues.title: Implementation of remote ACP incompatible with remote MCP
source_issues.evidence: When connected to a remote project over SSH, Zed launches MCP stdio instances locally instead of passing MCP configuration to the remote ACP agent. The ACP agent cannot see MCP tools, making the combined remote ACP + remote MCP workflow completely non-functional. Settings panel forces remote=false even when connected to remote instance.

signals.topic: Claude ACP agent cannot recover/resume old chat sessions from chat history list
signals.summary: When a new Claude ACP instance starts and user clicks an old chat in the history list, the session load fails with 'Resource not found' error, causing users to lose access to prior AI conversations.
aliases: old chat session cannot be loaded
session load error resource not found
signals.review_reason: Users lose access to their entire AI conversation history when using Claude ACP. This is a data loss issue for the primary AI chat feature — users cannot resume important prior conversations, directly blocking the workflow of iterative AI-assisted development.

source_issues.title: Editor claude-acp cannot recover old chats from list
source_issues.evidence: When a new Claude ACP instance starts and user clicks an old chat in the history list, the session load fails with 'Resource not found' error. Log shows session/load RPC request fails with code -32002. Users lose ability to continue prior AI conversations.

signals.topic: GitHub Copilot via Zed Agent causes excessive premium request usage (billing anomaly)
signals.summary: Single chat prompt with tool calls consumed 54 premium requests when it should have consumed only 3, an 18x overage due to Zed incorrectly creating new sessions per tool call.
aliases: tool calls creating extra sessions billing anomaly
signals.review_reason: Direct cost impact — users are being billed 18x more than expected for GitHub Copilot premium requests when using tool calls through Zed. This is a significant billing anomaly that causes unexpected financial loss. The same workflow in VS Code costs 3x less. Clear evidence of Zed incorrectly handling Copilot session management per tool call.

source_issues.title: Copilot: Unexpectedly high usage of premium requests from tool calls
source_issues.evidence: A single chat prompt with tool calls (e.g. web fetch) consumed 54 premium requests when it should have consumed only 3 (1 prompt x 3 multiplier for Opus 4.6). VS Code with the same setup correctly uses 3 premium requests. This is an 18x overage. Multiple new sessions are created per tool call as shown in Zed logs.

signals.topic: GitHub authentication prompt appears despite properly configured git-credential-manager
signals.summary: Despite having git-credential-manager properly configured and CLI Git working fine, Zed's Git UI prompts for username/password on HTTPS git projects, blocking fetch/push operations.
aliases: git credential manager not working in zed
github https auth broken in zed
signals.review_reason: Breaks core Git workflow in Zed's UI for HTTPS repositories. Despite having proper credential configuration that works in CLI Git and other tools, users cannot push/fetch through Zed without manual auth prompts. Blocks version control operations that are central to using Zed as a development environment.

source_issues.title: Getting prompted for GitHub login despite having git-credential-manager etc
source_issues.evidence: User has git-credential-manager properly configured and CLI Git works fine, but Zed's Git UI prompts for username/password on HTTPS git projects. This blocks core Git operations (fetch/push) through Zed's UI. Error logs show 'Not a directory (os error 20)' from repository.rs.
